selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: At the time described in this passage, what kind of Being does the human spirit turn toward in the Maghrib prayer?
questions.answer: It turns toward the One who never dies, never fades, and remains forever.

questions.question: What does saying Allah is the greatest do to the worshipper’s view of created things?
questions.answer: It lowers their hold over the heart and places Allah above them all.

questions.question: Why are the great changes in the world important in this passage?
questions.answer: They show signs of Allah’s power and remind the believer that creation is not permanent.

questions.question: What is being affirmed by saying that worship and help are for Allah alone?
questions.answer: It affirms that only Allah deserves worship and that only He is the real source of help.

questions.question: When the worshipper bows, what truth about the human self becomes clearer?
questions.answer: That the human self is weak, poor, and powerless on its own.

questions.question: Why is asking Allah alone for help spiritually significant?
questions.answer: Because it directs trust and need to the One who truly controls all affairs.

questions.question: What does the worshipper discover in prostration?
questions.answer: He finds Allah as the Eternal and Merciful One.

questions.question: Why does the passage end by praising Allah as exalted above every fault?
questions.answer: To affirm that Allah is completely beyond weakness, decline, and imperfection.

questions.question: What does the worshipper gain when he finds Allah as Merciful and Eternal?
questions.answer: He gains nearness, reassurance, and a lasting object of love and worship.

questions.question: What human quality is highlighted at the start of the passage about the spirit?
questions.answer: The spirit is described as naturally longing for lasting beauty.

questions.question: Which divine reality answers that need during Maghrib prayer?
questions.answer: Allah’s eternal and unchanging being answers it.

questions.question: Why does the worshipper verbally place Allah above temporary beings?
questions.answer: To affirm that created things are limited and should not hold the highest place in the heart.

questions.question: What is the purpose of folding the hands and standing before the Lord?
questions.answer: It is to enter worship with respect, submission, and readiness to serve.

questions.question: What three divine qualities are especially honored in that praise?
questions.answer: His perfection, His unmatched beauty, and His vast mercy.

questions.question: Why is that pairing important for a believer’s life?
questions.answer: It unites devotion and dependence so that both the heart’s love and the heart’s need are directed to Allah.

questions.question: What comparison between human beings and Allah is emphasized in bowing?
questions.answer: Human beings are limited and needy, while Allah is infinitely mighty and powerful.

questions.question: In the description of prostration, what happens to everything besides Allah?
questions.answer: It is set aside so the heart can focus fully on Him.

questions.question: What does glorifying Allah at the end of the passage protect the believer from believing?
questions.answer: It protects the believer from imagining that Allah has any defect, weakness, or decline.

questions.question: What is the main spiritual movement described at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: The heart moves from created things that vanish to Allah, who is everlasting.

questions.question: What does this image suggest about human fitrah?
questions.answer: It suggests that people are made to seek what is truly enduring, not what quickly passes.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the meaning of praising Allah after standing in prayer?
questions.answer: It means recognizing His perfection, beauty, and mercy.

questions.question: What does seeking help from Allah alone train the believer to do?
questions.answer: It trains the believer to rely on Allah as the final support in every need.

questions.question: In this passage, what does exclusive worship say about Allah’s dominion?
questions.answer: It says His rule and authority belong to Him alone without any partner.

questions.question: What inner shift happens in prostration according to the passage?
questions.answer: The person leaves attachment to everything besides Allah and turns fully to Him in love, awe, and humility.
